W.note: Clean 5-7-5 (Night's edge, pearl-thin cloud = 5; lit from beneath by the sun, = 7; seen by no one else = 5), and the nacreous cloud lit from below after sunset is accurately evoked, though the closing turn is a familiar lonely-witness move.

X.note: Lines count 4-7-4 (Mid-win-ter ridge = 4; wind runs through a lens of cloud = 7; that does not move = 4), so the frame is short on both ends, though the lenticular cloud that stays still while wind passes through it is a true and striking observation.

Y.note: Exact 5-7-5 (First snow on the ridge = 5; the lens holds, wind running through = 7; and the cloud stays still = 5), and it is a lenticular cloud, but it nearly repeats X's image and the snow anchor sits oddly with the cloud's phenomenon.

Z.note: Lines count 5-7-5 (Rare cloud, mother-pearl = 5; blooms where the sky holds no sun, = 7; gone before the name. = 5), and gone before the name lands the rarity as a feeling, while mother-pearl gestures at nacreous cloud and blooms is a soft, familiar verb.
